title: 1 m cross-section features: keep the flood hydraulics (xs_vel, xs_omega_q) and add channel-shape features
description:
Sean (2026-11-26): keep the flood-hydraulics features for the 1 m data, and add features that describe channel shape. Settle the list before the one-pass extraction spec (rf-lxa.3), so the national 1 m pass keeps the raw section data they need.

## Kept for 1 m: flood hydraulics (in the ML registry since rf-zmy.10, in no recipe)
- `xs_vel`: mean velocity at the mean annual flood, V = Q / A on the reach's median section, with the flood stage from Manning (n = 0.045, S = reach gradient, Q = MAF); log10 m/s. Your "constricted channel flows faster" feature.
- `xs_omega_q`: unit stream power at the mean annual flood over the Manning flood width, rho g Q S / w_q; log10 W/m2.
Why they wait: on the 8 m DEM the Manning flood stage has a median of 0.3 m, far below what the DEM resolves, so V and omega were mostly noise (partial rank agreement with LiDAR 0.14-0.21 after flood and slope are removed; docs/cross-sections.md). On 1 m LiDAR the stages 0.5-5 m become measurable. Caveat: LiDAR does not see below water, so the area under the water surface at capture time is missing; measure stages from the water surface and record the capture flow/date where known, or add an estimated under-water area (e.g. from at-a-station hydraulic geometry) and say so.

## Channel-shape features to evaluate (from the 1 m sections; per reach: median and spread over the sections every 50 m or less)
- Shape exponent: fit w(h) ~ h^b (or A(h) ~ h^m) over the low stages: b ~ 1 for a V, ~0.5 for a parabolic/U channel, -> 0 for a box or slot (vertical walls).
- Form factor A / (w * d) at a stage: 0.5 triangle, 0.67 parabola, 1 rectangle.
- Width-to-depth ratio at bankfull (or a fixed low stage), and hydraulic radius R = A / P.
- Bankfull estimate: the stage where the width-stage curve breaks (width jumps as water leaves the channel); bankfull width and depth from it.
- Entrenchment ratio (Rosgen): flood-prone width (at twice the bankfull depth) / bankfull width; separates gorges and slots from channels with a floodplain.
- Bank steepness: mean slope of each bank within the low-stage band, and the share of bank steeper than ~60 degrees (bedrock walls).
- Asymmetry: left vs right bank slope and width (cut bank vs bar; one-sided bedrock wall).
- Along-reach variability: coefficient of variation of the low-stage width and depth (pool-riffle vs uniform), frequency of pinch points (sections under ~0.5 of the reach median width), the existing constriction index at low stages.
- Bed roughness from the 1 m long profile: spread of the detrended thalweg elevation (boulder gardens, steps), next to the steps/drops in rf-lxa.3.
- Valley shape for context: valley floor width-to-height ratio (Vf) at 10-20 m stages (the 8 m xs_w10/xs_w20/xs_wall kept for continuity).
Evaluate each with the rf-zmy.10 protocol (separation within style x size, partial correlation with existing terrain features, grouped CV with paired repeats and LORO) on the rf-lxa.2 benchmark tile before the national pass, and keep only those that add information; but store the raw section data (rf-lxa.3) so others can be computed later without a rerun.
notes:
rf-lxa.2: sample cross-sections at 1 m within +-150 m of the reach, 5 m DEM beyond (10-20 m stages). The x05y07 sub-area (20 x 21 km, Hokitika / Toaroha / Kokatahi, box 1437000 5229000 1457000 5250000) streams in ~10 s; data/analysis/lidar-bench/variants holds the 1 m-routed reaches there.
Done (commit 658ea08, docs/cross-sections-1m.md): 14 rf-zmy.10 tiles, 92,582 LiDAR reaches >= 2 km2, 5,389 positives; sections every 25 m re-centred on the 1 m channel (86 % kept). Keep list (10): valley x1_w10, x1_w20, x1_wall, x1_vf (replace 8 m xs_*); shape x1_b, x1_ffbf; banks x1_bank, x1_steep; bed x1_rough, x1_dropconc. CV style-matched gain: +0.0086 vs gbm_terrain, +0.0024 vs gbm_xsec, +0.0110 vs logit_plus (all 10/10); LORO 0.874 -> 0.886 (10/11 regions). x1_vel: flood stage now resolved (median 1.0 m) but 91 % explained by MAF and gradient, adds nothing -> registry only, computed after the merge from the stored median stage table; x1_omega_q dropped (rank-identical). Storage: raw section profiles, 651 heights per section (1 m to +-150 m, 2 m to +-500 m), int16 cm deltas + nodata mask, Feather v2 zstd, ~620 B/section; defaults taken: 25 m spacing on reaches >= 1 km2 = 4.4 GB national (+~17 % on 8 m fallback). Cost on 2 m tiles ~70-85 min national.

title: 1 m LiDAR coverage audit: where it exists, capture years, gaps, fallback rule and water surfaces
description: Part of the 1 m LiDAR rebuild: before designing the national run, know where 1 m LiDAR exists. title: 1 m LiDAR pipeline design and benchmark tile: resolution, tiling and halo, memory, disk, run time
description: Part of the 1 m LiDAR rebuild: design the national pipeline for this machine (4 cores, 15 GB RAM, a fixed disk allowance) and measure it on one benchmark tile with many guide reaches (e.g. Kaimai/Bay of Plenty or a West Coast gorge tile). Decide: routing resolution (1 m everywhere is ~270 billion cells; 2 m or 5 m routing with 1 m sampling for gradients and cross-sections is the likely answer: measure both), tile size and halo (rf-t26.11 lakes and inflows across tile edges, rf-3ri.6 buffer), streaming the 1 m COGs per tile without keeping the national 1 m on disk, what intermediate rasters to keep, resumability, peak memory (stay well under 15 GB; the 8 m tiles peaked at ~12 GB), and the run time estimate for the country. Compare the benchmark tile's reaches with the aerial photos and the LINZ river lines (offset distance) at each resolution.
notes:
2026-11-26: disk is the tight constraint here: about 9 GB free of the session allowance (data/ is 16 GB, of which data/nz/tiles 2.9 GB). A 64 km tile of 1 m DEM is ~4 billion cells (16 GB as float32 uncompressed), so stream the COGs in small blocks, keep only resampled/derived rasters per tile and delete as the run goes; measure the per-tile disk peak on the benchmark tile. Run it in a fresh session if the allowance cannot fit it.
2026-11-27 from rf-lxa.1 (docs/lidar-coverage.md): benchmark tile x05y07 (West Coast, Hokitika-Harihari: 14 guide rivers, 153 guide km, 99.9% LiDAR, worst line drift: national line 48 m off the Hokitika near the gorge, 244 m median below it) or x12y16 (Kaimai/BoP: 103 guide km, holds the kaimai reference area, Kaituna/Wairoa/Tuakopae samples and the Lake Rotorua nodata hole). Never route from COG overviews (LERC max error 0.1 m on overviews vs 0.001 m full res; overviews quantise flats). Mosaic = 377 GB, 424 COGs, 233 billion valid cells; reads ran 2-3.9 M cells/s here, so full-resolution national reading is 16-30 h unless more parallel or limited to near-channel windows. Lake interiors are nodata (Taupo 494 km2): fill flat at the LiDAR water level. 1 m D8 paths are 15-29% longer than 8 m lines (smooth before measuring length). 1 m attributes must come from 1 m (or fine) routing, not from sampling along today's 8 m lines.

title: Rainfall accumulation per catchment (IMERG + ECMWF, gauge-scaled)
description:
GOAL
For every catchment nationwide, keep a running total of rainfall (mm and m³) over the past x hours. x is any whole hour from 1 to 24; default windows are 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24h. Totals add up down the river network, so each catchment includes everything upstream.

SOURCES (all behind one RainfallSource interface; record which source supplied each hour)
1. NASA GPM IMERG (main source for observed rain; replaces JAXA GSMaP, decided 2026-11-19; free NASA Earthdata login)
   - Half-hourly 0.1° grids (V07, cell centres on x.x5°), summed in pairs into hourly totals.
   - IMERG Early Run (about 4 h latency) for the most recent hours; IMERG Late Run (about 14 h) overwrites Early for the same hour when it lands; IMERG Final Run (about 3.5 months, gauge-calibrated) overwrites Late when it exists (history and validation).
   - The newest ~4 h have no IMERG yet: ECMWF short-lead hours cover them (see 2a), with the product recorded per hour.
2. ECMWF IFS open data (first-class source, not a fallback)
   - 0.1° grid, published since 20 Oct 2026; one forecast run every 6 hours.
   - Two uses: (a) an alternative observed-window source built from the first few forecast hours of each run (the short-lead hours), so it can be compared with IMERG side by side; (b) a forecast metric: rain expected in the NEXT x hours.
   - Check the time step of the precipitation fields. If they come in 3-hourly steps, either split them into hours (and document how) or read the hourly ecmwf_ifs data from the Open-Meteo S3 bucket (s3://openmeteo, CC-BY 4.0).
   - Which source each metric uses is set in config, so either can be the main source for observed rain.

GAUGE COMPARISON + SCALING
- Read hourly rain-gauge data from regional council Hilltop servers. Start with West Coast, Canterbury and Tasman.
- For each source, compare grid totals with gauge totals per region over a rolling 30-day window, and compute a scale factor.
- Guard rails: a minimum-rainfall threshold before computing a ratio, limits on how far a factor can move, and a minimum number of gauges. With too few gauges, use factor = 1.0.
- Calculate factors separately for IMERG and for ECMWF.
- Store with every hourly slot: the raw value, the scaled value, the factor, and the factor version.

DOCUMENTATION (required)
- docs/rainfall-scaling.md: the method, regions, thresholds, limits, update schedule, and how a factor is traced back to the gauges and dates it came from.
- A table of the factors in use, plus a history of changes to them.
- A validation report for one past West Coast storm: catchment totals from IMERG and ECMWF against gauges, before and after scaling.

PIPELINE
- Build once: a sparse matrix of grid cell -> catchment, weighted by the share of each cell's area inside the catchment.
- Every hour: one matrix multiplication gives mm per catchment; multiply by catchment area to get m³.
- Keep the last 24 hourly values per catchment in a rolling buffer; any window is the sum of the last x values.
- Add totals down the network, working from upstream catchments to downstream ones, so each catchment includes everything upstream.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Any x from 1 to 24 can be configured; the defaults work as listed.
- Both sources run through the same interface and can be switched in config.
- Each hour shows which product it came from (IMERG Early / Late / Final, or ECMWF), and a later IMERG run overwrites an earlier one for the same hour (Late over Early, Final over Late).
- Scaling runs with its guard rails; raw and scaled values are both kept.
- The scaling documentation and the storm validation report are committed.
- The ECMWF forecast metric for the next x hours is available.

ACCESS NEEDED (check before starting each child)
- IMERG needs a NASA Earthdata login (Sean registers; an Earthdata bearer token goes only through the environment's credential flow for the GES DISC host, never in files or commits).
- Network hosts to allow as needed: NASA GES DISC (gpm1.gesdisc.eosdis.nasa.gov, plus urs.earthdata.nasa.gov if the token flow needs it), ECMWF open data (data.ecmwf.int) or the Open-Meteo S3 bucket, and the council Hilltop servers (West Coast, Canterbury, Tasman).

title: ML feature: cross-sectional height-to-area (channel constriction -> flow speed)
description:
Sean: add a model parameter for the cross-sectional height-to-area of each river segment: a constricted channel carries the same flow faster (and steeper, pushier water) than a wide one.

Proposal:
- Cross-sections from the DEM perpendicular to the channel every ~50-100 m along each reach (1 m LiDAR where it exists, else the 8 m DEM). Per section: width w(h) and flow area A(h) at stages h above the channel/water surface (e.g. 1, 2, 5 m), bank height (relief within e.g. 50 m), and the shape (V vs U vs flat floor).
- Per reach features (median and a high quantile over its sections): cross-sectional height-to-area (bank height / A at a reference stage), width at stage, A at the stage that carries the mean annual flood or median flow, and derived hydraulics: mean velocity V = Q / A, unit stream power omega = rho g Q S / w (Q = MAF from the flood statistics, S = reach gradient), and a constriction index (narrowest section width / reach median width) for pinch points.
- Check against what already exists so the new feature adds information: valley_width_m (HAND <= 5 m area per metre), confinement_ratio (valley width / estimated bankfull width) and height_to_width (gorge depth / valley width) in reaches.py / ml.py (features valley_w, confine). Run the grouped CV (ml cv) with and without the new features and report AUC / style-matched AUC changes.
- Limits: 8 m cells cannot resolve channels narrower than ~16 m (most creeks), so stages below ~2 m and narrow gorges are only meaningful on LiDAR; LiDAR DEMs show the water surface, not the bed (area is above the water surface). Flag reaches where the section is unresolved.
- Wire into the national pipeline (reach metrics at nz tiles or a separate pass from the DEM, then ml table, models, viewer Details) and document the method in docs/flow-routing-algorithms.md or a new docs page.
notes: 2026-11-26: blocks rf-lxa (national rebuild on the 1 m LiDAR DEM). Settle it in the 1 m pipeline design (rf-lxa.2) before the national run, so everything is extracted in one pass.
close_reason: Method and features done (xsec.py, docs/cross-sections.md; recipes gbm_xsec, logit_xsec; 240 tests). Sections every 50 m, +-40 m wide, stages 1-20 m, walls within 50/150 m; on the 8 m DEM only the 10-20 m stages and the walls are resolved (rank agreement with LiDAR 0.78-0.94); 1-2 m stages, V/U shape and Manning velocity / stream power are not (Manning flood stage median 0.3 m). Sample CV (14 tiles, 43% of positives, paired, 10 repeats): gbm_xsec vs gbm_terrain style-matched AUC +0.0053 (10/10), style x size +0.012; LORO better in 9 of 11 regions. Not run nationally at 8 m by Sean's decision (2026-11-26): the cross-sections are extracted at 1 m in the national LiDAR pass (rf-lxa, spec rf-lxa.3), where the small stages and the flood hydraulics become measurable.
